headline: 尤薩傳記與芭蕾新評
context: 英國作家 Gerald Martin 為秘魯諾貝爾文學獎得主尤薩（Mario Vargas Llosa）撰寫的新傳記出版，追溯他從年輕時的左翼立場，一路轉向晚年親近柴契爾夫人的政治轉折。另一邊，倫敦皇家歌劇院也迎來首席芭蕾伶娜瑪麗安内拉‧努涅斯（Marianela Nuñez）的首場個人秀《Timeless》，44 歲的她技巧依然精湛，獲得劇評盛讚。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: This stylish biography of the author traces his journey from left to right, and from ‘posh Lima’ to Cricklewood “At what precise moment had Peru fucked itself up?” Those words on the opening page of Conversation in the Cathedral announced the arrival of a writer who understood that national history could become the organising principle of fiction. At precisely the moment when Latin America was discovering the intoxicating possibilities of magical realism – a form whose exuberance had an elective affinity with revolutionary politics, collapsing the distinction between the marvellous and the possible – Mario Vargas Llosa plumped for old-fashioned realism instead. It was a question of sensibility as much as politics, Gerald Martin suggests in this chatty yet coolly analytical biography. He traces the path of a novelist who began by dissecting oligarchy with surgical precision and ended happily dining among its ranks, completing one of literary history’s most spectacular political migrations – from the hard left to the hard right, over the course of half a century. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Royal Opera House, London In what is officially her first solo show, the star principal marshals technically peerless performances from a tremendous company in finely chosen repertoire Is there such a thing as being too perfect? Marianela Nuñez is certainly one of the most perfect ballerinas around. At 44, she still has superlative technique and absolute command. She can reel off a fiendish string of fouettés (as in tonight’s extract from Le Corsaire), whipping her leg in circles, and then come to a gentle standstill, the smoothest brakes you ever saw. It is absolutely frictionless; it is beauty and capability and egoless self-possession. And this might seem an unfair ask, but do we sometimes also need a little grit? Timeless is Nuñez’s first solo show. Not truly solo, but she’s the star, it’s her choice of repertoire, and she does everything “just right”, paying tribute to the Royal Ballet, the company she joined at 16, and its choreographers: Frederick Ashton, Kenneth MacMillan, Christopher Wheeldon, Wayne McGregor. She also offers an amazing showcase of the company’s dancers and generously allows them to shine, so much so that Matthew Ball and Mayara Magri dancing the balcony scene from Romeo and Juliet is an absolute highlight, Magri giddy as she watches her Romeo swoop manfully around the stage. Akane Takada and Calvin Richardson are tender in a duet from McGregor’s Infra, and Fumi Kaneko and Lukas B Braendsrød dance Wheeldon’s serene After the Rain – although they can’t fill the long phrases in the exquisite way Nuñez once did with Thiago Soares. 尤薩傳記與芭蕾新評

英國作家 Gerald Martin 為秘魯諾貝爾文學獎得主尤薩（Mario Vargas Llosa）撰寫的新傳記出版，追溯他從年輕時的左翼立場，一路轉向晚年親近柴契爾夫人的政治轉折——這被視為文學史上最戲劇性的政治轉向之一。

同一天，倫敦皇家歌劇院也迎來首席芭蕾伶娜瑪麗安内拉‧努涅斯（Marianela Nuñez）的首場個人秀《Timeless》。44 歲的她技巧依然精湛，這場演出獲得劇評盛讚。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 7 月 30 日發佈的兩篇報導。
voice_text: 文化這邊今天有兩則評論。第一則是秘魯諾貝爾文學獎得主尤薩的新傳記出版，作者追溯他從年輕時的左翼立場，一路轉向晚年親近柴契爾夫人，是文學史上少見的政治大轉向。另一則是倫敦皇家歌劇院，首席芭蕾伶娜瑪麗安内拉‧努涅斯首度舉辦個人秀。她今年四十四歲，技巧依然精湛，這場演出獲得劇評盛讚。
